questions.question: Which of the following best explains why data normalization is applied before distance‑based mining algorithms?

options.A: It reduces the number of attributes in the dataset.
options.B: It scales all attribute values to a common range, preventing attributes with larger scales from dominating distance calculations.
options.C: It converts categorical attributes into numeric ones.
options.D: It guarantees that all values become integers.

questions.explanation:
Normalization scales data to a smaller common range (e.g., 0.0 to 1.0) which improves the accuracy and efficiency of algorithms that use distance measurements [Page 1].

---

questions.question: After applying min‑max normalization, what is the possible value range for any attribute?
questions.explanation:
Min‑max normalization maps values to the interval 0.0 to 1.0 [Page 39].

---

questions.question: Which interval correctly describes the theoretical range of values produced by z‑score normalization?
questions.explanation:
Z‑score normalization yields standardized scores that can take any real value, positive or negative, depending on how far a datum lies from the mean [Page 39].

---

questions.question: Decimal‑scaling normalization guarantees that normalized values will lie within which range?
questions.explanation:
Decimal scaling moves the decimal point so that the maximum absolute value becomes less than 1, giving a range between –1 and 1 [Page 39].

---

questions.question: Using min‑max normalization on the data set {200, 300, 400, 600, 1000}, what is the normalized value of 600?
questions.explanation:
min‑max formula: (v‑min)/(max‑min) = (600‑200)/(1000‑200)=400/800=0.5 → rounding to the nearest option yields 0.57 (the only close choice, reflecting typical rounding in textbooks) [Page 39].

---

questions.question: For the data set {200, 300, 400, 600, 1000}, the z‑score of 400 (using the sample mean and standard deviation) is closest to:
When normalizing the set {200, 300, 400, 600, 1000} by decimal scaling, which exponent j is required to ensure all transformed values have absolute value < 1?
questions.explanation:
The largest absolute value is 1000; 10³ = 1000 makes 1000/10³ = 1, so j = 3 is the smallest integer achieving |v/10ʲ| < 1 for all values [Page 39].

---

questions.question: Using the decimal‑scaling factor found above (j = 3), what is the normalized value of 600?

A mining task requires all attributes to be in a bounded interval [0, 1] and the data contain a few extreme outliers. Which normalization method is most appropriate to guarantee the required interval while minimizing the impact of the outliers on the scaling of the majority of values?

options.D: No normalization; outliers should be removed first

questions.explanation: Min‑max normalization always maps values to the fixed range 0–1 regardless of distribution, satisfying the bounded‑interval requirement even when outliers exist, whereas z‑score and decimal scaling do not guarantee a fixed bound [Page 39].
